text: On Peter Singer's sentientist view, the fundamental ground of moral status is...
choices: rational autonomy and the capacity to set and pursue ends
membership in a community of mutual recognition and address
the capacity for suffering and well-being (sentience)
the possession of an immortal soul
explanation: Singer, following Bentham, holds that sentience -- the capacity to suffer and fare well -- grounds moral status, so equal interests get equal weight regardless of species. Rational autonomy is the personhood/Kantian criterion, mutual recognition is the relational account, and the soul view is theological -- all rivals Singer rejects.
